previous_statement: Let B be that convex coordinate box and let z,z' in B. Since the domain and codomain split as icalH direct-sum calH and alpha+beta is the canonical identification with calX, identify the identity derivative with (alpha,beta) maps to alpha+beta. Along gamma(t)=z'+t(z-z'), the Banach-space fundamental theorem of calculus gives p_V(z)-p_V(z')-(z-z')=integral_0^1 (Dp_V(gamma(t))-I)(z-z') dt, hence its norm is at most theta||z-z'||. Therefore (1-theta)||z-z'||<=||p_V(z)-p_V(z')||<=(1+theta)||z-z'||, proving injectivity and bi-Lipschitz control. At each z, Dp_V(z)=I+E_z with ||E_z||<=theta<1, so the norm-convergent Neumann series sum_{n>=0}(-E_z)^n is its inverse and has norm at most (1-theta)^{-1}. The finite-dimensional C^1 inverse function theorem makes p_V a local C^1 diffeomorphism. Injectivity makes the local inverses agree on overlaps; since a local diffeomorphism is open, these glue to a C^1 inverse on p_V(B), so p_V:B to p_V(B) is a C^1 diffeomorphism.
new_statement: Let B be the open convex coordinate box, with max norm, and J_0(alpha,beta)=alpha+beta. Put E_z=J_0^{-1}(Dp_V(z)-J_0); child 1.2.1.2 gives sup_B||E_z||=theta<=1/4. For z,z' in B, the finite-dimensional fundamental theorem of calculus along gamma(t)=z'+t(z-z') gives p_V(z)-p_V(z')-J_0(z-z')=integral_0^1 (Dp_V(gamma(t))-J_0)(z-z')dt. Applying J_0^{-1} yields ||J_0^{-1}(p_V(z)-p_V(z'))-(z-z')||_max<=theta||z-z'||_max, and hence (1-theta)||z-z'||_max<=||J_0^{-1}(p_V(z)-p_V(z'))||_max<=(1+theta)||z-z'||_max. Thus p_V is injective and bi-Lipschitz (equivalently in the original codomain norm, since J_0 is a fixed isomorphism). At each z, Dp_V(z)=J_0(I+E_z); the norm-convergent series sum_{n>=0}(-E_z)^n inverts I+E_z and has norm at most (1-theta)^{-1}, so Dp_V(z) is invertible. The finite-dimensional C^1 inverse function theorem makes p_V a local C^1 diffeomorphism and therefore an open map. Its injectivity makes the local inverses agree, yielding a C^1 inverse on p_V(B); hence p_V:B to p_V(B) is a C^1 diffeomorphism.
